deviations: Knesset web hosts (main.knesset.gov.il, fs.knesset.gov.il, m.knesset.gov.il) redirect to a geo-block page ('maintenance-page-geo'), including the law and bill PDFs the sheet pointed to; a read-through proxy (r.jina.ai) was also blocked. In their place I used (a) the NYU Faculty Digital Archive's mirror of Divrei HaKnesset full-day PDFs (Jewish Settlements Archival Project, collection handle 2451/64459) as Knesset records, extracting text locally with a PDFKit script, and (b) Wikipedia articles on the 13th, 14th, 24th, 25th, 34th, 35th and 37th governments for government composition, as the sheet allows when the Knesset site is unreachable.

Pages opened that turned out to be about a court case or to discuss how a court treated an enactment, closed and not used: Kipa 1173669 (a High Court ruling on the incapacity amendment, enactment 8); Calcalist local_news/r1o9s8gec (discusses the Supreme Court's treatment of Basic Law: Human Dignity and Liberty; its vote figures were therefore not used); PalQuest node/36118 (discusses Supreme Court rulings applying that Basic Law; its vote figures not used).

Web-search result snippets exposed court outcomes for enactments 2, 5, 6, 8 and 9 (the Bergman case, HCJ 8260/16, a ruling on the 'Hauser compromise', HCJ 2412/23, HCJ 5658/23) and a Detroit Jewish News/JTA item of 25 July 1969 mentioning a court decision; none of those pages was opened and nothing from the snippets was used.

The Hebrew Wikisource consolidated pages for Basic Law: The Government and Basic Law: The Judiciary carry bracketed tags and notes referencing court cases (a tag 'בג״ץ 2412/23' and a parenthetical beside s. 16(ב1); a note on s. 15(ד1) saying the amendment was annulled). I used only the statutory text and publication metadata from those pages and disregarded the annotations; enactment 9's text was taken from the gazette page itself.

Sources outside the sheet's examples that I used, and why: WIPO Lex record 15283 for the 1994 text of Basic Law: Freedom of Occupation and its entry-into-force date (the Wikisource page shows only the 1998-amended text of s. 8); a copy of Sefer HaHukkim 3066 page 548 hosted on the Israel Democracy Institute's media server, used solely as a copy of the gazette page; the r.jina.ai proxy to read the body of a Jerusalem Post article of 19 July 2016 that the direct fetch returned without text. Press reports used for tallies and reading dates: Times of Israel, Globes, Jerusalem Post, Davar, Maariv, Calcalist, Walla, Kipa, Kikar HaShabbat, Srugim, JDN (Knesset spokesperson release), Algemeiner/Reuters.

Nevo pages for plenum and committee protocols and for bills (ה״ח) require a login; only Nevo's law pages were readable. A search-engine snippet of a Nevo-mirrored protocol (28 Jan 1992) was corroborated from the NYU copy of the same record before use.

Not found in any permitted source, cells left blank: enactment 1's final tally and cross-party votes (no 17 March 1992 sitting in the NYU mirror; usable press all discussed court treatment) and its exact first-reading date (bounded only as before 28 Jan 1992); enactment 2's final tally (the record shows a voice vote, 'נתקבל', with no count) and exact first-reading date (bounded to 23 Jan–17 Feb 1969); enactment 3's and enactment 8's party breakdown of the final vote.

Texts not obtained as published in the gazette: enactment 2 (Knesset PDF geo-blocked; absent from Wikisource and Nevo), coded from the committee chair's reading of the amended text into the Knesset record of 19 Feb 1969; enactment 6's main section (coded from Nevo's note on the indirect amendment, ס״ח תש״ף 2845 p. 420, and press descriptions of the 23 Dec 2020 deadline); enactment 8 (coded from Nevo's and Wikisource's consolidated text of s. 16, with immediate_effect flagged low-confidence). Explanatory notes were unreachable for enactments 1, 3, 4, 5, 8 and 9; for 7 and 8 press quotations of the notes were used.

The 1994 NYU plenum PDF's roll-call lists for the section-8 vote were jumbled by right-to-left extraction; I used only the announced totals and speakers' statements, not individual names from the roll-call.
No file in the sheet's folder other than coding-sheet.md was opened, listed or searched; temporary PDF and text extracts were kept in the session scratchpad.
